Palace's picture is more positive if Sage's comments about Mateta, Henderson and Tomiyasu hold: a fit Mateta gives Palace their focal-point striker back after the 4-0 opening win, while Tomiyasu adds defensive solidity at a moment when Lyon are dealing with their own fitness questions at the back. A Palace side closer to full strength, facing a Lyon team missing its most advanced attacking threat six days after a damaging league defeat, supports the draw-or-away structure of this pick better than it supports backing the home side outright.

### Statistical Core Predictions-Sports-Prime

Statistical coverage is partial. Both sides have played a single UEFA Europa League league-phase match this season, so no sourced home and away split is available for this fixture in the 22-metric target format; building a venue-specific Core from a one-match sample would overstate its reliability. The Matchday 1 scorelines, current absences and the context set out above are the genuine sourced evidence used for this pick, and the metrics that would normally fill this table remain unavailable from a competitive, venue-specific sample at this early point in the season.

## Market assessment and risk

The clearest risk is that Palace's three headline returns (Mateta, Henderson, Tomiyasu) are based on a manager's pre-match comment rather than a confirmed teamsheet, and any of the three could still be held back as a precaution; Starting11's broader tracker lists all three as out, which is a genuine source conflict worth flagging rather than resolving silently. A second risk is home advantage itself: Lyon start at Groupama Stadium and, Openda's absence aside, still have enough attacking quality to beat a Palace side that is also missing several squad players. Weighing those risks against the case for the pick, the X2 structure (draw or Palace win) only needs Lyon to fail to win outright, a lower bar than needing Palace to win the match themselves, which is the main reason the pick is retained despite the uncertainty in Palace's own fitness news.

The published market price is **1.68**, which carries a raw implied probability of **59.52%** using 1 / 1.68. That percentage is the market threshold the pick needs to clear, not a claim that it equals the true chance of the outcome.

## Conclusion

Weighing the team news and Matchday 1 evidence above against the published price, the retained call for Lyon vs Crystal Palace stays Crystal Palace or Draw (X2) at 1.68, unchanged from the original publication package.
